questions.worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,z)\le y\le {u}_{2}(x,z)\}.

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,z)=0,\,{u}_{2}(x,z)=1+x+z.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le z\le 2x+1\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2x+1}[{\int }_{0}^{1+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2x+1}{\int }_{0}^{1+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=(-1)+(2x+1)=2x.
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2-x\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}2x[y]_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-x}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}{[z]}_{z=0}^{z=2-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}(2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(\frac{32}{3}-8)-0 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le x,\,0\le z\le 2-x\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}[{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3x[y]_{y=0}^{y=x}dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3x(x-0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3{x}^{2}\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3{x}^{2}\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-x}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}{[z]}_{z=0}^{z=2-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}(2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & ={[2{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(16-12)-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}xyz\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-2z},\,0\le y\le x\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}xyz\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy\,dx\,dz.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}xyz\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}xz{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}xz(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\,dx\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{x}^{3}z\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2x}}{x}^{3}z\,dx\,dz & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2z}}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-2z}}\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{4}(4-2z)^{2}z\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4z-4{z}^{2}+{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4z-4{z}^{2}+{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z & =\frac{1}{2}{[2{z}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{z}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(8-\frac{32}{3}+4)-0 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}4xy\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{1-z}\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $z=1-{x}^{2},$ in the first quadrant.
questions.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4xy\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}2x[{y}^{2}]_{y=x}^{y=\sqrt{1-z}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x(\,(1-z)-{x}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/95a2b4e28dbfae5ce447b3b975b2f74bf04883441217f42a24636970948402a0.png)

  

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}2x\,dx]dz+{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}-2{x}^{3}\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-z}}dz+{\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-z}}dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[-(1-z)^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Example: 
                    Representing a Triple Integral as a Mixed or Repeated Integral
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the missing limits in the repeated integral below

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
\int_{\ast}^{\ast} 
f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x
$$

where $R$ is the type III region defined as

$$
R=\left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2, \: 0 \leq y \leq z+xz \right\}.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z)  \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: u_1(x,z) \leq y \leq u_2(x,z) \big\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/0603bed12c6af74e46544d8bebc52362aed95a9a5ad7418ea4faaf228f3b5241.png)

 

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d y \right] \,\textrm d A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u_1(x,z) = 0, \qquad u_2(x,z)  = z+xz.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{S} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{z+xz} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D =\left\{ (x,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2 \right\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{2x+2}[{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{x}^{2x+2}{\int }_{0}^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Evaluating a Mixed Integral
canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{x}} 2y\: \mathrm{d}y \right ]  \mathrm{d}A,
$$

given that $D$ is the region in the $xz$-plane bounded by the lines $z=0,$ $x= 1$ and the line $z =x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}2y\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to calculate this double integral, we plot $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/1d102b63c3deb8121ea88cdc994b9410cf28f9c3bb29abc5ea4a14d7e1e7c389.png)

 

Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[z]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type III Region
canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 8xy  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt x \right\},
$$

and $D$ is the finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the line $x=1,$ and the line $z=x$ in the first quadrant.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 8xy \, \textrm{d}V
=
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{x}} 8xy\: \mathrm{d}y \right ]  \mathrm{d}A.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}8xy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}4x[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}4x(x-0)\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}4{x}^{2}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/1d102b63c3deb8121ea88cdc994b9410cf28f9c3bb29abc5ea4a14d7e1e7c389.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4{x}^{2}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{2}(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & ={1}^{4}-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/b0817c04ee57a8352f8f56a4c232668d415c1573e37a81729752d65c0fb9e1c1.png)

 

Evaluate the triple integral 
$\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 36z^2  \: \mathrm{d}V$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/0584c95ae22135288f08fc8d0ef472aae867eccecf958c65e82eb311da69a1ae.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 5-x-z \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/365451aa395e91cee59199b048ed59ce1fba2ee8ee569fc460ef8fe9bf3bcdfd.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 5-x-z \big\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
\displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} 36z^2 \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{5-x-z} 36z^2 \: \mathrm{d}y \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}x.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{5-x-z}36{z}^{2}\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{5-x-z}36{z}^{2}\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}36{z}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=5-x-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}36{z}^{2}(5-x-z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(180{z}^{2}-36x{z}^{2}-36{z}^{3})\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(180{z}^{2}-36x{z}^{2}-36{z}^{3})\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(180{z}^{2}-36x{z}^{2}-36{z}^{3})\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[60{z}^{3}-12x{z}^{3}-9{z}^{4}]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(51-12x)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(51-12x)\,dx & =[51x-6{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(51(1)-6(1)^{2})-0 \\  & =45\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.problem:
Let's evaluate the triple integral 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 2xz  \: \mathrm{d}V
$$

where the region $R$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/9b00702b941e40061ff242e63c0d1b33642cce9aefc1ffa9f88e9d94cd02897a.png)

 

The region $R$ is a type III region. So, our first task is to describe this region fully.

We start by drawing an arrow parallel to the $y$-axis that 

- enters the region through the *left* surface $y=0,$ and

- leave the region through the *right* surface $y=6-x-z,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/5102f786fa91eb862fd3f5ef8f0b2cbc85fbdff6fc616f86f498aa0da8088f14.png)

 

So, our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 6-x-z \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/30f320f2e77c95c13e59bc3fdd6b273d1ad367018af3cd12bd6d2fde7cc09132.png)

To evaluate our triple integral, we start by expressing it as a mixed integral:

$$
\iiint\limits_R 2xz \:\textrm{d}V
=
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A
$$

Now, since the region $D$ is a type I *plane* region, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 6-x-z \big\},
$$

and therefore, our mixed integral can be written as the following repeating integral:

$$
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_0^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A
=
\int_{0}^{3} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x
$$

Evaluating this using the usual methods, we get

$$
\int_{0}^{3} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x = 15.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\iiint\limits_R 2xz \:\textrm{d}V = 15.
$$
